acceptance_criteria: The status of ARCH-20260925-060 and of Ruling D20 is reported before anything is written.
One property is chosen and the reason stated.
Every field of the repaired stamp is true of what it names.
The guard fails on a stamp naming an ancestor that is not the declared property, demonstrated by breaking it.
Which assertions are provable on CI and which only locally is stated.
B22's fourth recurrence is recorded with D20 as its resolution.
Suite passes; count reported before and after.
assumptions: The stamp's intended property is that it names the commit the document describes. Confirm against how the stamp has been maintained rather than assuming.
The suite count on main is 1003; the guard compares against the tree under test, not a remembered number.
constraints: FIRST: report whether ARCH-20260925-060 was ever transported or executed. A response file was not found; if the command file is present unexecuted, this command supersedes it by quotation — do not run both. If it is absent, this is the first issue and say so.
SECOND: report whether Ruling D20 is already recorded. If it is, cite it and do not duplicate it.

CHOOSE ONE PROPERTY FOR THE STAMP and state why. Either (a) it names the tip of main, guarded by equality with main — correct only between a merge and the next merge; or (b) it names the commit the document describes, guarded by that commit being the most recent to modify the document, with the count true of that commit's tree. Do not leave both.
REPAIR THE STAMP so every field is true of what it names. A count under an as-of-sha label that the sha never had is a hand-stamp wearing a generated fact's clothes (convention 24).
EXTEND THE GUARD to test the declared property, and PROVE IT BY BREAKING IT: a stamp naming an ancestor that is not the declared property must FAIL. That is the stamp on main now.

CARRY THE CI LESSON: whatever this guard needs from git must resolve under CI's PR checkout. Resolve locally first, origin/main second. State which assertions are provable on CI and which only locally, and do not write a guard that goes red on a correct stamp.
The deliberate break now runs only where a local main exists. State that limitation as declared and bounded — it is honest and it is the reason CI proves the guard by a weaker test.
Do NOT weaken the existing three assertions. Extend them.
Do NOT reopen B22 as a new defect. Record this as B22's fourth recurrence with D20 as its resolution.
Every count re-derived against the tree (convention 24).
